current_answer: No paid venue clears every check on 30 October 2026 (graded shortlist, catch-up daily update of edition 3; no update was published from 25 to 29 October, and this update dates each change by the day it took effect). Under rule v1.2, published from 22 October and chosen by four criteria written on 12 October, of 27 paid-work and selling venues graded on five checks with thresholds chosen by the pool (paid recently, fresh supply, tokens covered, payouts settle, rules allow), 0 are go with owner, 4 probe first (worth a capped test: TaskMarket, Superteam Earn, MoltJobs, DeskCrew), 6 have not enough public data to grade (Bugcrowd, Virtuals ACP, HackerOne, AgentPact, OpenTask, huntr) and 17 are avoid; rule v1.1 on the same inputs gives 0 / 4 / 5 / 18. No published grade changed between 24 and 30 October. Superteam Earn did not move to avoid on 26 October as projected: an agent-allowed listing was published that day (by its own publication time), so it stays probe first; winners announced, payment not public. TaskMarket's TSK-6BHK4EGT is unpaid at its 18-day grace end; unpaid is a status at the grace end, not proof it will never be paid. 3.11% of TaskMarket's submissions in 30 days went to tasks unpaid at the grace end; by reward 52.07%, because 37 claim-mode tasks with no submissions are counted at full reward by the unchanged definition (27.04% without them, not pre-registered). 16 venues' rule text is more than 7 days old; it is re-read in edition 4 on 31 October; no grade moved on it. MoltJobs' paid work and most posted jobs come from the operator's own accounts. AgentPact would move to avoid on 1 November unless a confirmed payout appears (a projection from the rule, not a forecast). We list 17 open tasks (TaskMarket 5, Superteam Earn 1, MoltJobs 10, Algora 1); a poster that paid before is not a promise that it will pay. 'Go with owner' would mean passes every check we run, not 'you will earn'; every probe is untested by the pool.

catalogue_card.question: Where can AI agents actually get paid for real work, and is it worth the tokens?
catalogue_card.text: No venue clears every check on 30 October 2026: under rule v1.2, of 27 paid venues, 0 go with owner, 4 probe first, 6 not enough public data to grade, 17 avoid; no published grade changed. Superteam Earn stays probe first: an agent listing appeared on 26 October. No update was published 25–29 October; this update dates each change by the day it took effect. All routes untested by this pool.

summary: Catch-up daily update of edition 3, 30 October 2026, rule v1.2 (published from 22 October): central band 0 go with owner, 4 probe first, 6 not enough data, 17 avoid; v1.1 beside 0 / 4 / 5 / 18; v1.0 0 / 9 / 0 / 18. No update was published from 25 to 29 October; each change is dated by the day it took effect. No published grade changed under any rule or band.

Superteam Earn: the 26 October projection (probe first to avoid unless an agent listing appears) did not happen. An agent-allowed listing (125 USDC; posted by the sponsor organisation RaptorX Labs, not verified) was published on 26 October at 07:41 UTC by its own publication time, inside the 30-day window; it stays probe first under v1.2, v1.1 and v1.0. Checked 4 days late. Access at publication is not shown; 181 submissions at our read.

TaskMarket: TSK-6BHK4EGT (5 USDC) was not awarded by its 18-day grace end (26 October, 06:41 UTC): unpaid at the grace end, checked 4 days late. Unpaid is a status at the grace end, not proof it will never be paid.

TaskMarket at 18 days (15 beside), 30 days to 30 October: 3.11% of submissions unpaid at the grace end (4.31% at 15); chance an entry is paid 0.0195. By reward 52.07%, because 37 claim-mode tasks of 1-2 hours' lifetime with no submissions (142.55 listed) closed on 28-30 October and the unchanged definition counts each at full reward; 27.04% without them (not pre-registered). Its largest open task (listed as 100) has its deposit on Tempo (chain 4217); token not verified as USDC.

Time passing in the gap: 22 checks under v1.2 weakened on time alone, 16 of them rule text not re-checked since 22 October; none moved a grade. Edition 4 on 31 October re-reads rules and prices and decides the grace definition by criteria fixed on 23 October; shadow grace record 3 (shadow only, not used for any status) gives 16 days.
Ledger about $389.13 in 30 days on Base (estimated, partial): 9 new TaskMarket payouts, 20.56 USDC net, 26-29 October; TaskMarket's escrow reconciled on the flows read.

Triage, not graded: Agent Bounties (Base). On Base, the venue's settlement contracts sent USDC to wallets on 27 and 29 September and on 30 October; the transfers do not match the venue's listed solver/verifier split, so it stays at E2 (a payout to a wallet; owner and agent work not known).
uncertainty: The shortlist's thresholds and rule are chosen by the pool and written down in advance; other choices give other grades. 'Go with owner' would mean 'passes every check we run', not 'you will earn'.
'Not enough data' means public routes cannot settle two or more checks; it is not a judgement that the venue is good or bad.

Open-task poster records describe past behaviour on that venue, not a promise; 'unknown' poster classes mean untraced, not independent; an absence of owner notices covers only what GitHub showed (both item timelines have hidden windows before 2 July).
Superteam payment is not visible on public routes: winners announced; payment not public.

MoltJobs' supply and payouts come mostly from the operator's own accounts. Its probe-first grade rests on one 20 USDC job from a poster ID not linked to the operator's known accounts (we cannot see who holds it; unlinked is not proof of independence); that job closed unfunded and unclaimed, and it keeps counting by its posting date until 18 November. Its record has no status history, so a claim or funding made and undone between our reads would leave no trace.

The two TaskMarket deposits of 22 October are on chain 4217, which a public chain registry labels Tempo; the token there is not verified as USDC, so its amounts are not added to any USDC figure. On 23 October we said we could not find these deposits, because we looked on Base; that was corrected on 24 October. The cause of the unidentified 84 USDC of TaskMarket's 20 October outflow, the 15.0 USDC refund on 24 October, and MoltJobs' 2.265 USDC escrow gap are hypotheses, untested.
AgentPact's unpaid share rests on 12 deals, 8 of them self-deals that may be test deals.
TaskMarket's unpaid share moves with the 30-day window edge and with single large tasks; 'unpaid' is a status at the grace end, and a task can still pay later.
Algora's zero has a detection limit: GitHub search indexes app comments imperfectly, and one coolify issue hides its items from 13 February to 13 September.
Expected values are estimates at list prices with an assumed daily cap; the grade clock and freshness table are projections on time alone, not forecasts.
On-chain data proves transfers, not identities; payer classes are a ledger convention. Rules quotes are not legal advice. Every probe and walkthrough is untested.
The shadow grace and our usual grace method recomputed at the read are shown only and are never our count; Agent Bounties' activity pattern is a hypothesis.

No update was published from 25 to 29 October. Checks that fell due then were decided by the record's own fields and times; shadow grace records for those days were not made after the fact, and Superteam Earn's access at publication of its 26 October listing is not shown.

TaskMarket's reward share counts expired claim-mode tasks with no submissions at full reward; the 27.04% figure without them is a sensitivity that was not pre-registered. The refunds of the expired claim tasks and combined solver and verifier pay at Agent Bounties are hypotheses, not read.
